question: Should OpenClaw define a backend-neutral distributed scheduler/job ownership contract in core or plugin APIs, route Redis/BullMQ-style orchestration to a ClawHub plugin on current seams, or defer the broad layer to narrower cron/session/runtime trackers?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but backend boundary, worker failure semantics, config/credential shape, observability, cron ownership, and core-versus-plugin policy are maintainer architecture choices.

options.title: Design backend-neutral contract
options.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, observability, and security review before backend-specific code lands.

options.title: Route queue backend to plugin
options.body: Keep core Tasks/TaskFlow canonical and ask Redis/BullMQ durable executor work to ship through ClawHub unless a plugin proves a narrow missing core API.

options.title: Defer to narrower trackers
options.body: Let cron HA, external session storage, distributed runtime, K8s worker auth, and execution-backend issues settle first, then revisit whether a broader queue layer remains necessary.

recommendation.title: Design backend-neutral contract
recommendation.body: Define shared queue/state, worker claiming, retries/backoff, dead-letter semantics, cron support, observability, and security review before backend-specific code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest live issue signal plus the clearest queue/cron architecture history for choosing the boundary.
